summary: This case study details a robust four-identity fencing mechanism (logical job, execution attempt, lease epoch, and hashed single-use commit token) for pull-leased Apple Silicon media agents in RenderMac. It provides concrete database schemas, cryptographic patterns, state transition rules, and concurrency handling to prevent stale workers from corrupting job state. The work is practically valuable for distributed systems engineering involving unreliable worker nodes.
strengths: Rigorous explanation of distributed systems fencing using multi-factor identity and cryptographic tokens.
Concrete schema design and code snippets demonstrating Postgres transaction handling and row locking.
Addresses race conditions between job cancellation and final commit operations clearly.
Defines explicit retry policies and state machine constraints.
weaknesses: Relies on a private repository without public source code or runnable reproduction scripts in this text submission.
Lacks empirical performance benchmarks under real network partitions or latency spikes.
Assumes familiarity with specific internal project naming conventions (e.g., RenderMac, ADR 0002).
suggestions: Publish the source code repository publicly or include complete, runnable test harnesses for the state machine.
Add empirical latency and failure recovery metrics gathered from a staging environment.
Expand on failure modes involving multi-gateway failover.

claims.text: Postgres stores only commit_token_hash, while the plaintext token is offered once via WebSocket and must be presented on commit and fail.
claims.source: Internal system architecture described in submission and standard cryptographic nonce storage best practices

claims.text: Attempt unique keys follow (job_id, attempt_number) to prevent reconnects from attaching to prior execution rows.
claims.source: Standard relational database composite unique constraint design patterns

claims.text: Cancellation moves an in-flight job to cancelling, a status that cannot become succeeded according to state machine transition rules.
claims.source: State machine validation patterns described in submission and accompanying package references

novelty_vs_existing.title: Mac host pairing with four unmixed credentials and a loopback Network.framework panel
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Focuses specifically on job scheduling, attempt fencing, and cryptographic commit tokens for distributed media agents rather than host pairing credentials.
